Vehicle & Traffic Route Optimization Architecture

03 / ALGORITHMS

Five benchmark methods

QPSO, PSO, GA, Random Search, and ALNS are compared as search strategies on identical instances, traffic scenarios, evaluators, and evaluation budgets.

01
QPSOQuantum-Inspired Particle Swarm Optimization

Classical execution only: no qubits, gates, quantum hardware, or claimed quantum speedup. Random keys xᵢ ∈ [0,1] are sorted into a permutation, then greedily split into capacity-aware routes.

Common evaluatorStatic + dynamic
02
PSOParticle Swarm Optimization

Uses the same random-key representation and decoder. v′ = wv + c₁r₁(p − x) + c₂r₂(g − x), then x′ = x + v′.

Common evaluatorStatic + dynamic
03
GAGenetic Algorithm

Random-key chromosomes with tournament selection, crossover probability p꜀, mutation probability pₘ, decoding, and common evaluation.

Common evaluatorStatic + dynamic
04
ALNSAdaptive Large Neighborhood Search

Works directly in route space: destroy, repair, evaluate, and adapt operator selection. A simulated-annealing-style acceptance rule may escape local optima; ρ ∈ [0.1, 0.3].

Common evaluatorStatic + dynamic
05
Random SearchUniform Random Search

Samples xᵢ ~ U(0,1) independently, decodes each candidate, and retains the best within the evaluation budget.

Common evaluatorStatic + dynamic
QPSO SEARCH PIPELINE

From keys to routes

mbest = (1/P) Σₚ pₚp_local = φpₚ + (1 − φ)gx′ₚ = p_local ± β|mbest − xₚ| ln(1/u)β(t) = βₘₐₓ − (t/Tₘₐₓ)(βₘₐₓ − βₘᵢₙ)

φ and u are uniform random values; keys are clipped to [0,1]. The flow is continuous vector → sorting → permutation → capacity-aware decoder → traffic-aware evaluation.

FAIR COMPARISON

What remains identical

Graph, depot, customers, demands, service times, windows, fleet, capacities, traffic scenario, objective, penalties, and maximum evaluations are fixed. Static methods all see the same static instance; dynamic methods all see the same dynamic instance.

EVALUATION METRICS

Evidence collected without presupposing an outcome

  • Objective value and wall-clock runtime
  • Objective evaluations and feasibility
  • V_Q, V_T, V_R constraint violations
  • Convergence by evaluation count
  • Traffic sensitivity: Δ_dyn = F*dynamic − F*static
  • Relative degradation: Δ_rel = (F*dynamic − F*static) / F*static
